_comment: large-datasets, staged as a top-level named subgraph. Owner, 2026-09-20: 'maybe not core skill, sub-graph of skills to deal with "large data sets"'. It exists because a capability was missing from BOTH neighbours: `materialize-remote` (in folio-assist-core) answers 'may we take this, and what does holding it cost', and nothing answers the question before it -- how do you ENUMERATE a corpus, and how do you ask it for a SUBSET? Every source answers differently and none of it is guessable, so without a declared descriptor an agent asked for 'the WPRO style guides' must be told the API by a human every time. NOT in folio-assist-core, deliberately: core is the CONTENT layer, and this is about sources the instance will never hold. NOT in cat-harness: it is not about the harness either. It is the third thing, which is what earns it a subgraph rather than a directory inside one.

assets.description: The two worked descriptors and why the second one is what makes the abstraction real.

directories.description: `source-descriptor` — how to enumerate a corpus and ask it for a subset. `artifact-store` — where an artifact too large for the site tree goes, as a DECLARATION rather than a hardcoded host, per the owner's 'make tool that can be done another way potentially if not github cdn'.

One descriptor per corpus. TWO today and the pair is deliberately far apart, because one example is a special case with an interface drawn round it: WHO IRIS (items stand alone; three identifier systems; paged REST) and Lean mathlib (declarations need their import closure; one identifier system; a local module graph). The `subsetIsSelfContained: false` row exists only because the second was written.
The instruction bodies. A separate id from every other `cat-harness` graph in the checkout: overrides match on the entry's id, so reusing one would REPLACE that graph rather than add to it.

`gen-id-lookup.ts` builds the prefix-sharded identifier lookup over a catalogue's REFERENCED nodes (`bun run id-lookup`, gated by `id-lookup:check`), and `bench-id-lookup.ts` measures it at full WHO IRIS scale on a seeded synthetic corpus, in Chromium. Bean `4pm8`: the Pagefind decision waits on this measurement.

The identifier lookup a reader uses: `lookup.js` (plain ES module, no dependencies), a one-form `index.html`, and one generated index per corpus (`who-iris/`: `manifest.json` plus JSON shards keyed by id prefix, each under 64 KiB). JavaScript, so it lives HERE and never under the plain docs pipeline, which is 'no extensions. no fancy. no js (if possible)'. The `who-iris/` index is generated by `scripts/gen-id-lookup.ts`; edit the catalogue, never the shards.
